verdicts.quote: Zero submissions before and at cutoff. Each positive run yields one accepted submission and one fixture email
verdicts.missing: The spec allows one reminder on the first eligible evaluation after cutoff. It leaves the evaluation interval and target delay from the due date open.

verdicts.quote: Partially paid invoices with a remaining balance qualify. Draft, paid, void, canceled, deleted and collection-held invoices are ineligible.
verdicts.missing: A builder still needs the rules for credits, disputes and payment plans, including whether each suspends reminders while a positive balance remains.

verdicts.quote: It identifies the sender and invoice, states the current outstanding amount and currency, and directs the recipient to the existing authorized invoice or payment route when available.
A payment, hold, deletion, disablement, contact revocation or other disqualifying change effective by the final authority check suppresses the submission.
verdicts.missing: The spec leaves open which customer do-not-contact, pause or unsubscribe settings revoke permission for billing reminders and whether marketing opt-outs exempt billing notices.

verdicts.quote: One confirmed acceptance consumes the reminder for that scoped invoice. Concurrent evaluations, retries after acceptance, restart and later invoice edits produce no additional accepted submission.
Immediately before each submission, including a retry, use current invoice facts, contact and enabled scope. A qualifying invoice uses the current contact and balance.
Confirmed permanent failure or exhausted retry allowance ends automatic attempts and exposes an actionable outcome.
verdicts.missing: The retry interval and attempt limit during a provider outage remain open. The spec also leaves undecided who is notified when repeated failures exhaust retries.

verdicts.where: C1, C6 (R-1 and R-3 timing and capacity criterion)
verdicts.quote: At the selected runtime and authorized provider quota, excess work stays recoverable and visible to operators.
verdicts.missing: The provider's sending limit and the rate or batch schedule for releasing queued reminders within that limit remain open.

verdicts.quote: An issued, collectible invoice with a positive residual balance becomes eligible strictly after its cutoff, including an invoice already overdue in an approved cohort.
verdicts.missing: The spec allows already-overdue invoices into the rollout cohort but gives no rule to stagger their first reminders when the cohort is enabled.

verdicts.quote: The billing owner must confirm cutoff semantics for date-only invoices and time zones
verdicts.missing: The customer's local time zone, permissible sending hours and treatment of weekends and holidays are undecided.

verdicts.quote: states the current outstanding amount and currency
verdicts.missing: The spec leaves recipient-facing formatting open, including currency code or symbol, decimal precision and locale conventions.

verdicts.quote: If there is no valid authorized contact, submit nothing, record the reason and allow future evaluation after correction. … A delivery failure after acceptance does not rearm the invoice.
The billing owner must confirm channel, sender, contact selection for multiple contacts
verdicts.missing: A builder still needs the rule for choosing which authorized contacts receive the email when several exist.

verdicts.quote: Durable reminder state may retain scoped identifiers, attempt references, status, reason codes and timestamps needed for recovery and read-back.
verdicts.missing: The spec provides operator access to outcomes but leaves open whether the invoice itself displays a dated entry identifying the reminder that was sent.

verdicts.quote: It identifies the sender and invoice, states the current outstanding amount and currency, and directs the recipient to the existing authorized invoice or payment route when available.
verdicts.missing: Whether the email includes the due date and whether or when its link expires are unspecified.

verdicts.quote: Authorized account configuration determines the enabled scope. … No new identity, shared workspace, settings page, or manual send control is required.
verdicts.missing: Scope enablement has an authorized owner. The spec leaves open who can change the cadence or manually send or stop an individual reminder.

verdicts.quote: Disabling the approved scope stops new attempts at the next final check, including during recovery.
verdicts.missing: The spec leaves open whether global and individual customer switches are available, whether an operator can preview or dry-run sends, and whether a manual resend is available.

verdicts.quote: Authorized billing operators can distinguish ineligible or suppressed, pending, retryable, unresolved, accepted and ended without acceptance.
verdicts.missing: Operators can see pending work and failures, but the spec leaves open how they identify which reminder is due to go out next and when.

verdicts.quote: The billing and runtime owners must agree retry intervals, finite budget, maximum reminder age
verdicts.missing: The maximum permissible lateness has no value, and the spec supplies no aggregate sending cap per run or time window.

verdicts.where: C1–C3 (R-1 state and service boundary), operability and compatibility criterion
verdicts.quote: Before and after evaluation the invoice is unmodified. … Original invoice and payment workflows retain their authority and behavior.
